title: The Isma'ilis
hook: a Shia community led today by a living Imam, the Aga Khan, known for development work

segments.voice: Yesterday, Shia communities today: the followers of Ali, from Baghdad to Lucknow, praying toward the same Ka'bah.

What happens when a question comes up that nobody in the first centuries ever faced? A new medicine. A new kind of work. A family that has moved to a country with different laws. Muslim communities have their own ways of answering. Some open the books of the schools. Some ask a mufti. Some ask a marja'. One community turns to a living Imam, a descendant of the Prophet's family, whom they recognize as the guide for their own time. His title is the Aga Khan. The community is the Isma'ilis.
screen: `A QUESTION NOBODY FACED BEFORE.` → `BOOKS, MUFTI, MARJA'.` → `A LIVING IMAM.`

segments.voice: Isma'ilis are Shia Muslims who trace their line of Imams through Isma'il, a son of the Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, and they take their name from him. Twelver Shia followed a different son, which is where the two branches part. The Isma'ilis described here hold that the line of Imams has never been broken, and that there is always a present Imam, the Imam of the time. They point to a verse in surah al-Nisa, in Pickthall's words: "Obey Allah, and obey the messenger and those of you who are in authority". For them, those in authority include the Imam. Sunni scholars read the same words differently, as rulers or people of knowledge. Each reads it within its own tradition. Isma'ilis gather in a jamatkhana, a house for the community's prayer and meeting. In South Asian communities, devotional songs called ginans are part of that life. Isma'ilis speak of the outward form of faith and its inward meaning, and see the Imam as a guide to both. Then the work. The Imam has built institutions grouped as the Aga Khan Development Network: schools, hospitals, rural support, care for historic buildings, help in places of poverty, open to people of every faith. Isma'ilis explain this as faith that cares for life in this world as well as the next. Volunteering, giving time and skill, is woven through the community's life.
screen: `THROUGH ISMA'IL, SON OF JA'FAR.` · `THE IMAM OF THE TIME.` · `JAMATKHANA AND GINANS.` · `SCHOOLS, CLINICS, VILLAGES.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one place that served you without asking who you were, a school, a clinic, a library, a shelter, and one person who worked there. Stay with that picture for a few breaths and let gratitude be simple. If you pray, thank Allah for that place in your own words.
The Isma'ilis. Shia Muslims who follow a living Imam, today the Aga Khan, gather in the jamatkhana, and are known for development work open to everyone. Today's word.
Your line: a living imam. A guide for this time, and work open to everyone. Tomorrow, converts and reverts.

options: To a living Imam, today the Aga Khan, whom they see as the guide for their own time.
Only to old law books; they hold that no living person can guide them today.
To a council of scholars, elected fresh by a community vote every single year.

notes: This describes the Nizari Isma'ilis, who follow the Aga Khan; other Isma'ili communities (for example the Musta'li Bohras) follow a different line and have no present Imam in the same sense. The teach says 'the Isma'ilis described here'; a Keeper may want a clearer line on this.
No count of Imams, no dates and no succession details are given, because the outline's text does not supply them; the Aga Khan is named only by title.
The list of AKDN fields (schools, hospitals, rural support, historic buildings) should be confirmed against AKDN's own description.
The reading of 4:59 as including the Imam, and the Sunni reading as rulers or people of knowledge, should be checked by scholars of each.
